tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

/-! ## Places (MM-03.3.2, A5) -/

/-- Holder of an authority (A4) or owner of a place (A5): a frame or a place. -/
inductive Holder where
  | frame (f : Nat)
  | place (p : Nat)
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Logical place (MM-03.3.2: `Place { id, parent?, frame, kind }`). Its identity is its index
in `P`. The field `frame` of MM-03.3.2 is generalised by `owner` (A5): a place is owned by a
frame or by another place (owned storage). A part has the owner of its parent (`WF3`). `kind`
is not interpreted: MM-03.3.2 gives no values for it. -/
structure Place where
  parent : Option Nat
  owner : Holder
  kind : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- `parent` link of the place with index `i` (MM-03.3.2). -/
def parentOf (P : List Place) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (P[i]?).bind (·.parent)

/-- `partOf P p q` (MM-03.3.2, logical composition): `p` is a place of `P` and `q` is `p` itself
or one of its ancestors along `parent`. -/
def partOf (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop :=
  p < P.length ∧ (p = q ∨ q ∈ chain (parentOf P) p)

instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (partOf P p q) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- Storage leaf (MM-03.3.2): a place without a strict part. -/
def isLeaf (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Prop := ∀ r < P.length, parentOf P r ≠ some l

instance (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Decidable (isLeaf P l) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _, _))

/-- `footprint P q` (MM-03.3.2): the leaves of `P` that are parts of `q`. -/
def footprint (P : List Place) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range P.length).filter fun l => decide (isLeaf P l ∧ partOf P l q)

/-- Two places overlap when their footprints share a leaf (MM-03.3.2). -/
def overlap (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop := ∃ l ∈ footprint P p, l ∈ footprint P q

instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (overlap P p q) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∃ _ ∈ _, _))

/-- Structural disjointness (MM-03.3.2): neither path is a part of the other. -/
def structurallyDisjoint (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop := ¬ partOf P p q ∧ ¬ partOf P q p

instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (structurallyDisjoint P p q) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

theorem mem_footprint {P : List Place} {q l : Nat} :
    l ∈ footprint P q ↔ l < P.length ∧ isLeaf P l ∧ partOf P l q := by
  simp [footprint, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range]

theorem footprint_congr {P P' : List Place} (hlen : P'.length = P.length)
    (hpar : parentOf P' = parentOf P) (q : Nat) : footprint P' q = footprint P q := by
  unfold footprint; rw [hlen]; congr 1; funext l
  exact decide_eq_decide.2 (by simp only [isLeaf, partOf, hpar, hlen])

/-! ## State `S3` (MM-03.3 §1) -/

/-- Initialisation state of a leaf (MM-03.3.3). -/

/-! ## O4 `transfer` (MM-03.3 §3, A4, A5) -/

/-! ## Shape of a value (J1) -/

/-- Children of the place `x` (MM-03.3.2), in index order. -/
def kids (P : List Place) (x : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range P.length).filter fun r => decide (parentOf P r = some x)

/-- Position of `r` in a list (its length if absent). -/
def posIn (r : Nat) : List Nat → Nat
  | [] => 0
  | a :: l => if a = r then 0 else posIn r l + 1

/-- The part of `dst` that corresponds to the part `r` of `src` (J1), searched within `n` steps:
`dst` for `src`; for another part, the child, at the same position among the children ordered by
index, of the place that corresponds to its parent. -/
def corrF (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) : Nat → Nat → Option Nat
  | 0, r => if r = src then some dst else none
  | n + 1, r => if r = src then some dst else
      match parentOf P r with
      | some p => if p < r then
          (corrF P src dst n p).bind fun p' => (kids P p')[posIn r (kids P p)]? else none
      | none => none

/-- The part of `dst` that corresponds to the part `r` of `src` (J1). -/
def corr (P : List Place) (src dst r : Nat) : Option Nat := corrF P src dst r r

/-- J1, « `dst` a la même forme que `src` (sous-arbres isomorphes) »: every part of `src` has a
corresponding part of `dst` with as many children, and every part of `dst` corresponds to a part
of `src`. Children are matched in index order (ordered isomorphism). -/
def SameShape (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) : Prop :=
  (∀ r ∈ List.range P.length, partOf P r src →
    OptP (corr P src dst r) (fun r' => (kids P r').length = (kids P r).length) False) ∧
  ∀ z ∈ List.range P.length, partOf P z dst →
    ∃ r ∈ List.range P.length, partOf P r src ∧ corr P src dst r = some z

instance (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) : Decidable (SameShape P src dst) := by
  unfold SameShape; infer_instance

/-- Holder within the value at `q` (A4): a place that is `q` or one of its parts. -/
def heldIn (P : List Place) (q : Nat) : Holder → Prop
  | .place r => partOf P r q
  | .frame _ => False

instance (P : List Place) (q : Nat) (h : Holder) : Decidable (heldIn P q h) := by
def RootPlace (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Prop := r < P.length ∧ parentOf P r = none

instance (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Decidable (RootPlace P r) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- First clause of B1: two distinct root places have disjoint footprints. Parts and their
containing places are not concerned. -/
def RootsDisjoint (P : List Place) : Prop :=
  ∀ r r', RootPlace P r → RootPlace P r' → r ≠ r' → ∀ l ∈ footprint P r, l ∉ footprint P r'

/-- Second clause of B1: the chain of origins of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root
authority of the root place of that leaf, an authority without origin whose footprint is the
footprint of that root place. -/
def RootChain (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[a]? = some y → l ∈ y.footprint → isLeaf s.P l →
    ∃ x z r, (x = a ∨ x ∈ s.ancs a) ∧ s.A[x]? = some z ∧ z.origin = none ∧ RootPlace s.P r ∧
      partOf s.P l r ∧ ∀ l', l' ∈ z.footprint ↔ l' ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- A4, "Une racine reste détenue par le propriétaire de son emplacement", a possession condition
that A1 keeps in `WF3`: an authority without origin is held by the owner of the root place of
every leaf it covers. -/
def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner

/-- `WF3` (A1, A4, B1, C3): well-formedness, the domain of admissible states, separate from the
safety invariant `Inv3`. Origins precede their derivations; footprints are made of existing
places; the stack is non-empty and without duplicates, below `nF`; owner frames are below `nF`;
owner places exist; a part comes after its parent and has its owner and its `dead` flag; every
active authority has a live holder (possession); B1: the chain of origins of an authority covering
a leaf ends at the root authority of its root place (`RootChain`); A4: a root is held by the owner
of its place (`RootHeld`). C3: the first clause of B1, `RootsDisjoint`, is not a clause: it holds
for every list of places (`rootsDisjoint_always`). -/
def WF3 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  (∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a → a < b) ∧
  (∀ (a : Nat) (x : Authority), s.A[a]? = some x → ∀ l ∈ x.footprint, l < s.P.length) ∧
  s.F ≠ [] ∧ s.F.Nodup ∧ (∀ f ∈ s.F, f < s.nF) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (f : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f → f < s.nF) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (o : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o →
    o < s.P.length) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
    ∃ pr : Place, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧ s.dead r = s.dead q) ∧
  (∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true → HolderLive s y.holder) ∧
  RootChain s ∧ RootHeld s

/-- The pass-1 exclusivity on effective modes (MM-03.3 §2, I1) is a theorem under the
strengthened I1 (A1). -/

/-! ## Projections of `WF3` -/

section WF3proj
variable {s : S3} (h : WF3 s)
include h

theorem WF3.origin : ∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y →
    y.origin = some a → a < b := h.1
theorem WF3.fp : ∀ (a : Nat) (x : Authority), s.A[a]? = some x → ∀ l ∈ x.footprint,
    l < s.P.length := h.2.1
theorem WF3.ne : s.F ≠ [] := h.2.2.1
theorem WF3.nodup : s.F.Nodup := h.2.2.2.1
theorem WF3.frames : ∀ f ∈ s.F, f < s.nF := h.2.2.2.2.1
theorem WF3.ownerFrame : ∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (f : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl →
    pl.owner = .frame f → f < s.nF := h.2.2.2.2.2.1
theorem WF3.ownerPlace : ∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (o : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl →
    pl.owner = .place o → o < s.P.length := h.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
theorem WF3.parts : ∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
    ∃ pr : Place, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧ s.dead r = s.dead q :=
  h.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
theorem WF3.poss : ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true →
    HolderLive s y.holder := h.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
theorem WF3.rootChain : RootChain s := h.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1
theorem WF3.rootHeld : RootHeld s := h.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2

end WF3proj

theorem WF3.ownerOf_aux {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) :
    ∀ n l r, l < n → partOf s.P l r →
      ∃ pl pr, s.P[l]? = some pl ∧ s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ pl.owner = pr.owner
  | 0, _, _, h, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, l, r, hl, ⟨hlen, hlr⟩ => by
    obtain ⟨pl, hpl⟩ : ∃ pl, s.P[l]? = some pl := ⟨_, List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.2 ⟨hlen, rfl⟩⟩
    rcases hlr with rfl | hc
    · exact ⟨pl, pl, hpl, hpl, rfl⟩
    cases hpo : parentOf s.P l with
    | none => rw [chain_none hpo] at hc; simp at hc
    | some p =>
      have hpar : pl.parent = some p := by simp [parentOf, hpl] at hpo; exact hpo
      obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hlt, ho, -⟩ := hw.parts l pl p hpl hpar
      rw [chain_cons hpo hlt] at hc
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hc with rfl | hc
      · exact ⟨pl, pr, hpl, hpr, ho.symm⟩
      · obtain ⟨pl', pr', hpl', hpr', he⟩ :=
          WF3.ownerOf_aux hw n p r (by omega) ⟨lt_of_getElem? hpr, .inr hc⟩
        rw [hpr] at hpl'; cases hpl'
        exact ⟨pl, pr', hpl, hpr', ho.symm.trans he⟩

/-- A part has the owner of the place it belongs to (A5, `WF3`). -/
theorem WF3.ownerOf {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {l r : Nat} (h : partOf s.P l r) :
    ∃ pl pr, s.P[l]? = some pl ∧ s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ pl.owner = pr.owner :=
  hw.ownerOf_aux (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) h

theorem WF3.deadOf_aux {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) :
    ∀ n l r, l < n → partOf s.P l r → s.dead l = s.dead r
  | 0, _, _, h, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, l, r, hl, ⟨hlen, hlr⟩ => by
    rcases hlr with rfl | hc
    · rfl
    cases hpo : parentOf s.P l with
    | none => rw [chain_none hpo] at hc; simp at hc
    | some p =>
      obtain ⟨pl, hpl⟩ : ∃ pl, s.P[l]? = some pl := ⟨_, List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.2 ⟨hlen, rfl⟩⟩
      have hpar : pl.parent = some p := by simp [parentOf, hpl] at hpo; exact hpo
      obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hlt, -, hd⟩ := hw.parts l pl p hpl hpar
      rw [chain_cons hpo hlt] at hc
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hc with rfl | hc
      · exact hd.symm
      · exact hd.symm.trans (WF3.deadOf_aux hw n p r (by omega) ⟨lt_of_getElem? hpr, .inr hc⟩)

/-- A part has the `dead` flag of the place it belongs to (A5, `WF3`). -/
theorem WF3.deadOf {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {l r : Nat} (h : partOf s.P l r) : s.dead l = s.dead r :=
  hw.deadOf_aux (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) h

theorem WF3.parent_lt {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {i o : Nat} (h : parentOf s.P i = some o) :
    o < i ∧ o < s.P.length := by
  simp only [parentOf] at h
  cases hp : s.P[i]? with
  | none => rw [hp] at h; cases h
  | some pl =>
    rw [hp] at h
    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hlt, -⟩ := hw.parts i pl o hp h
    exact ⟨hlt, lt_of_getElem? hpr⟩

theorem top_mem {s : S3} (h : s.F ≠ []) : s.top ∈ s.F := by
  unfold S3.top; cases hF : s.F with
  | nil => exact absurd hF h
  | cons f F => simp

/-- Frame stack `F` (MM-03.3.1): frame identities, current frame first. The parent of a frame
is the next element; the last element is the initial frame. -/
abbrev Frames := List Nat

/-- `ancestor F f₁ f₂` (MM-03.3.1): `f₁` is `f₂` itself or one of its ancestors in `F`, that is,
`f₁` occurs in `F` from the first occurrence of `f₂` on. -/
def ancestor (F : Frames) (f₁ f₂ : Nat) : Prop := f₁ ∈ F.dropWhile (· != f₂)

instance (F : Frames) (f₁ f₂ : Nat) : Decidable (ancestor F f₁ f₂) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∈ _))

/-! ## Parent chains

Places (by `parent`) and authorities (by `origin`) form forests whose identities are indices.
A chain only follows a link to a strictly smaller index; the fuel `k` only ensures
termination. -/

/-- Strict ancestors of `i` along the link `org`, nearest first. -/
def chainF (org : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → List Nat
  | 0, _ => []
  | k + 1, i =>
    match org i with
    | some o => if o < i then o :: chainF org k o else []
    | none => []

/-- Strict ancestors of `i` along `org` (fuel `i`, enough since the chain decreases). -/
def chain (org : Nat → Option Nat) (i : Nat) : List Nat := chainF org i i

theorem chainF_none {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i : Nat} (h : org i = none) :
    ∀ k, chainF org k i = []
  | 0 => rfl
  | _ + 1 => by simp [chainF, h]

theorem chainF_fuel (org : Nat → Option Nat) :
    ∀ k₁ k₂ i, i ≤ k₁ → i ≤ k₂ → chainF org k₁ i = chainF org k₂ i
  | 0, 0, _, _, _ => rfl
  | 0, _ + 1, i, h, _ => by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
    simp only [chainF]; split <;> simp
  | _ + 1, 0, i, _, h => by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
    simp only [chainF]; split <;> simp
  | k₁ + 1, k₂ + 1, i, h₁, h₂ => by
    simp only [chainF]; split
    · split
      · rw [chainF_fuel org k₁ k₂ _ (by omega) (by omega)]
      · rfl
    · rfl

theorem chain_none {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i : Nat} (h : org i = none) : chain org i = [] :=
  chainF_none h i

theorem chain_cons {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i o : Nat} (h : org i = some o) (hlt : o < i) :
    chain org i = o :: chain org o := by
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ : ∃ k, i = k + 1 := ⟨i - 1, by omega⟩
  simp only [chain, chainF, h, hlt, ↓reduceIte]
  rw [chainF_fuel org k o o (by omega) (Nat.le_refl o)]

theorem chainF_lt {org : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ k i j, j ∈ chainF org k i → j < i
  | 0, _, _, h => by simp [chainF] at h
  | k + 1, i, j, h => by
    simp only [chainF] at h; split at h
    · split at h
      · rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
        · assumption
        · exact Nat.lt_trans (chainF_lt k _ j h) ‹_›
      · simp at h
    · simp at h

/-- Every element of a chain is strictly smaller than its start: the walk along a chain
terminates (A7). -/
theorem chain_lt {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i j : Nat} (h : j ∈ chain org i) : j < i :=
  chainF_lt i i j h

theorem chainF_length {org : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ k i, (chainF org k i).length ≤ k
  | 0, _ => by simp [chainF]
  | k + 1, i => by
    simp only [chainF]; split
    · split
      · simp only [List.length_cons]; have := chainF_length (org := org) k ‹_›; omega
      · simp
    · simp

/-- A chain from `i` has at most `i` elements (A7: termination of the walk). -/
theorem chain_length (org : Nat → Option Nat) (i : Nat) : (chain org i).length ≤ i :=
  chainF_length i i

theorem chainF_congr {org org' : Nat → Option Nat} :
    ∀ k i, (∀ j ≤ i, org j = org' j) → chainF org k i = chainF org' k i
  | 0, _, _ => rfl
  | k + 1, i, h => by
    simp only [chainF]; rw [h i (Nat.le_refl i)]; split
    · split
      · rw [chainF_congr k _ fun j hj => h j (by omega)]
      · rfl
    · rfl

theorem chain_congr {org org' : Nat → Option Nat} {i : Nat} (h : ∀ j ≤ i, org j = org' j) :
    chain org i = chain org' i := chainF_congr i i h

/-- Two roots (elements without link) of one chain are equal. -/
theorem chainF_root {org : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ k i r r', r ∈ chainF org k i → org r = none →
    r' ∈ chainF org k i → org r' = none → r = r'
  | 0, _, _, _, h, _, _, _ => by simp [chainF] at h
  | k + 1, i, r, r', h, hr, h', hr' => by
    simp only [chainF] at h h'; split at h
    · rename_i o ho; simp only [ho] at h'
      split at h
      · rename_i hlt; simp only [hlt, ↓reduceIte] at h'
        rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h <;> rcases List.mem_cons.1 h' with rfl | h'
        · rfl
        · rw [chainF_none hr] at h'; simp at h'
        · rw [chainF_none hr'] at h; simp at h
        · exact chainF_root k _ r r' h hr h' hr'
      · simp at h
theorem transfer_partOf (s : S3) (src dst r q : Nat) :
    partOf (transferEff s src dst).P r q ↔ partOf s.P r q := by
  simp only [partOf, transfer_parentOf, transfer_len]

theorem mem_kids {P : List Place} {x r : Nat} :
    r ∈ kids P x ↔ r < P.length ∧ parentOf P r = some x := by
  simp [kids, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range]

theorem kids_nil_iff {P : List Place} {l : Nat} : kids P l = [] ↔ isLeaf P l := by
  constructor
  · intro h r hr hp
    have : r ∈ kids P l := mem_kids.2 ⟨hr, hp⟩
    rw [h] at this; simp at this
  · intro h
    exact nil_of_forall_not_mem fun r hr => by
      obtain ⟨hr, hp⟩ := mem_kids.1 hr; exact h r hr hp

theorem corrF_fuel (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) :
    ∀ n m r, r ≤ n → r ≤ m → corrF P src dst n r = corrF P src dst m r
  | 0, 0, _, _, _ => rfl
  | 0, m + 1, r, h, _ => by
    obtain rfl : r = 0 := by omega
    simp only [corrF]; split
    · rfl
    · split
      · split
        · omega
        · rfl
      · rfl
  | n + 1, 0, r, _, h => by
    obtain rfl : r = 0 := by omega
    simp only [corrF]; split
    · rfl
    · split
      · split
        · omega
        · rfl
      · rfl
  | n + 1, m + 1, r, h₁, h₂ => by
    simp only [corrF]; split
    · rfl
    · split
      · split
        · rw [corrF_fuel P src dst n m _ (by omega) (by omega)]
        · rfl
      · rfl

theorem corr_src (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) : corr P src dst src = some dst := by
  unfold corr; cases src <;> simp [corrF]

theorem corr_step {P : List Place} {src dst r p : Nat} (hr : r ≠ src)
    (hp : parentOf P r = some p) (hlt : p < r) :
    corr P src dst r = (corr P src dst p).bind fun p' => (kids P p')[posIn r (kids P p)]? := by
  obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ : ∃ n, r = n + 1 := ⟨r - 1, by omega⟩
  unfold corr
  simp only [corrF, hr, ↓reduceIte, hp, hlt]
  rw [corrF_fuel P src dst n p _ (by omega) (Nat.le_refl p)]

theorem getElem?_mem {l : List Nat} {i x : Nat} (h : l[i]? = some x) : x ∈ l :=
  List.mem_of_getElem? h

/-- The place corresponding to a part of `src` is a part of `dst` (J1). -/
theorem corr_partOf {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hd : dst < s.P.length) :
    ∀ n r r', r < n → corr s.P src dst r = some r' → partOf s.P r' dst
  | 0, _, _, h, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, r, r', hr, h => by
    by_cases e : r = src
    · subst e; rw [corr_src] at h; cases h; exact ⟨hd, .inl rfl⟩
    cases hp : parentOf s.P r with
    | none =>
      unfold corr at h
      cases r with
      | zero => simp [corrF, e] at h
      | succ m => simp [corrF, e, hp] at h
    | some p =>
      have hlt := (hw.parent_lt hp).1
      rw [corr_step e hp hlt] at h
      cases hc : corr s.P src dst p with
      | none => rw [hc] at h; cases h
      | some p' =>
        rw [hc] at h; simp only [Option.bind_some] at h
        have ih := corr_partOf hw hd n p p' (by omega) hc
        obtain ⟨hr'l, hr'p⟩ := mem_kids.1 (getElem?_mem h)
        have hlt' := (hw.parent_lt hr'p).1
        refine ⟨hr'l, .inr ?_⟩
        rw [chain_cons hr'p hlt']
        rcases ih.2 with rfl | hc'
        · exact List.mem_cons_self ..
        · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hc'

/-- A holder within the source moves to a part of the destination (J1, A4, A5). -/
theorem mvTo_part {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hd : dst < s.P.length) {h : Holder}
    (hh : heldIn s.P src h) : ∃ r', mvTo s.P src dst h = .place r' ∧ partOf s.P r' dst := by
  cases h with
  | frame f => exact hh.elim

1. `authority` est active **et dérivée** : une autorité sans origine est rejetée.
2. Elle est détenue par le cadre courant, ou détenue par un emplacement `p` sur lequel le cadre courant dispose de `Modify` exerçable.
3. Aucun descendant actif de l'autorité n'empêche sa libération ; aucune autre valeur encore utilisable ne doit perdre une ancre nécessaire.
4. Si l'autorité est stockée dans son emplacement détenteur, celui-ci est exempté du contrôle « cette autorité figure encore dans les ancres » **uniquement parce que l'effet supprime cette ancre simultanément**. Une ancre de même identité attachée par `depend` à un autre emplacement utilisable continue de bloquer le pas.
5. Les contrats applicables des abstractions restent satisfaits.

**Effet `ok`** : l'autorité devient inactive et ne peut plus être exercée. Elle est retirée des ancres de son emplacement détenteur lorsqu'elle y était stockée. Les modes effectifs de ses origines sont recalculés, permettant la restitution des droits non bloqués. Il n'y a aucune désallocation implicite. **Autre issue :** `reject`.

### O4 — `transfer(source, destination)`

**Préconditions**

1. `source` et `destination` sont utilisables, et le cadre courant dispose de `Modify` exerçable sur leurs empreintes pertinentes.
2. La source et la destination ont la **même forme de sous-arbres ordonnés**. Le `i`-ième enfant de chaque partie source correspond au `i`-ième enfant de la partie destination correspondante ; tous les nœuds sont appariés. L'identité d'un champ structurel est sa position, non un appariement arbitraire des enfants.
3. **Toutes** les feuilles de la source sont `Init` et **aucune** feuille de la destination n'est `Init`. Les empreintes source et destination sont disjointes.
4. Aucune autorité exclusive n'est dupliquée ; la validité des autorités dérivées et des projections actives est préservée.
5. **Aucune feuille en place de la source n’est épinglée**, statiquement (`K.Pinned`) ou dynamiquement (`pin`). Le stockage seulement **possédé** par la source, qui n’est pas lui-même déplacé par le transfert de cette valeur, n’empêche pas ce transfert.
6. Les dépendances de tous les emplacements encore utilisables qui suivent la valeur restent valides ; les contraintes de non-échappement et `AnchorOrder` sont vérifiées dans **l'état d'arrivée**, y compris les ancres transférées des emplacements possédés encore utilisables.
7. Toutes les autorités détenues déplacées, y compris celles du stockage possédé, satisfont `AnchorOrderHeld` dans l'état d'arrivée ; aucune autorité ne peut échapper à une ancre locale sous prétexte que sa valeur porteuse a été transférée.

**Effet `ok`** :

- chaque feuille source devient `Moved` et chaque feuille de destination correspondante devient `Init` ;
- chaque autorité détenue par la partie source `r` a pour nouveau détenteur la partie correspondante `corr(r)` de la destination, et non indistinctement la racine de destination ;
- les emplacements possédés par `r` passent sous la possession de `corr(r)` ; leurs racines suivent ce propriétaire conformément à `RootHeld` ;
- les dépendances de la valeur suivent les emplacements correspondants, sous les garanties de validité ; aucune autorité n'est créée ou dupliquée ;
- les emplacements de destination récupèrent les valeurs et droits transférés sans déplacer automatiquement le stockage dont une partie de la source n'est pas propriétaire.

**Autre issue :** `reject`. Le cas de `transfer` vers un résultat d'appel est soumis à ces mêmes règles.

Une structure partiellement initialisée peut être transférée **champ par champ**, seulement pour les champs individuellement transférables. Cela ne déstructure pas automatiquement une valeur qui possède du stockage **au niveau du contenant** : ce stockage reste au contenant si le contenant n'est pas transféré. Le passage entre structures dont les champs sont permutés est une conversion à traiter séparément, pas un `transfer`.

theorem nil_of_forall_not_mem {α : Type} : ∀ {l : List α}, (∀ a, a ∉ l) → l = []
  | [], _ => rfl

theorem pairwise_lt_range : ∀ n, (List.range n).Pairwise (· < ·)
  | 0 => by simp
  | n + 1 => by
    rw [List.range_succ, List.pairwise_append]
    exact ⟨pairwise_lt_range n, by simp, fun a ha b hb => by
      simp at hb; subst hb; exact List.mem_range.1 ha⟩

theorem filterMap_congr' {α β : Type} {f g : α → Option β} :
    ∀ {l : List α}, (∀ a ∈ l, f a = g a) → l.filterMap f = l.filterMap g
  | [], _ => rfl
  | a :: l, h => by
    simp only [List.filterMap_cons, h a (List.mem_cons_self ..),

import Ern.MM03
open Ern.MM03
namespace Ern.MM23

/-! ## Leaves of a transfer under `SameShape` (MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered isomorphism) -/

/-- A position in a list determines the member it was computed for (MM-03.3 O4.2: the identity
of a structural field is its position). -/
theorem posIn_inj : ∀ {l : List Nat} {r₁ r₂ : Nat}, r₁ ∈ l → r₂ ∈ l →
    posIn r₁ l = posIn r₂ l → r₁ = r₂
  | [], _, _, h, _, _ => absurd h List.not_mem_nil
  | a :: l, r₁, r₂, h₁, h₂, e => by
    simp only [posIn] at e
    by_cases e₁ : a = r₁ <;> by_cases e₂ : a = r₂
    · exact e₁.symm.trans e₂
    · simp only [e₁, e₂, ↓reduceIte] at e; omega
    · simp only [e₁, e₂, ↓reduceIte] at e; omega
    · simp only [e₁, e₂, ↓reduceIte] at e
      have h₁' : r₁ ∈ l := (List.mem_cons.1 h₁).resolve_left (Ne.symm e₁)
      have h₂' : r₂ ∈ l := (List.mem_cons.1 h₂).resolve_left (Ne.symm e₂)
      exact posIn_inj h₁' h₂' (Nat.succ.inj e)

/-- In a strictly increasing list, a value occurs at one index only. -/
theorem index_inj_of_lt : ∀ {l : List Nat}, l.Pairwise (· < ·) → ∀ {i j x : Nat},
    l[i]? = some x → l[j]? = some x → i = j
  | [], _, _, _, _, h, _ => by simp at h
  | _ :: _, hp, 0, 0, _, _, _ => rfl
  | a :: l, hp, 0, j + 1, x, h₁, h₂ => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at h₁; subst h₁
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_succ] at h₂
    exact absurd ((List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).1 _ (List.mem_of_getElem? h₂)) (Nat.lt_irrefl a)
  | a :: l, hp, i + 1, 0, x, h₁, h₂ => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_zero, Option.some.injEq] at h₂; subst h₂
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_succ] at h₁
    exact absurd ((List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).1 _ (List.mem_of_getElem? h₁)) (Nat.lt_irrefl a)
  | _ :: _, hp, i + 1, j + 1, _, h₁, h₂ => by
    simp only [List.getElem?_cons_succ] at h₁ h₂
    exact congrArg (· + 1) (index_inj_of_lt (List.pairwise_cons.1 hp).2 h₁ h₂)

/-- The children of a place are in strictly increasing index order (J1: children are ordered by
index). -/
theorem kids_lt (P : List Place) (x : Nat) : (kids P x).Pairwise (· < ·) :=
  (pairwise_lt_range P.length).filter _

/-- A strict part of `src` has a parent that is a part of `src` (MM-03.3.2, composition). -/
theorem partOf_parent {P : List Place} {r src p : Nat} (hr : partOf P r src) (hne : r ≠ src)
    (hp : parentOf P r = some p) (hlt : p < r) : partOf P p src := by
  have hc := hr.2.resolve_left hne
  rw [chain_cons hp hlt] at hc
  refine ⟨Nat.lt_trans hlt hr.1, ?_⟩
  rcases List.mem_cons.1 hc with h | h
  · exact .inl h.symm
  · exact .inr h

/-- One step of `corr` on a strict part `r` of `src` (J1): `r` has a parent `p`, a part of `src`,
and the image of `r` is the child, at the position of `r`, of the image of `p`. -/
theorem corr_parent {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst r x : Nat} (hr : partOf s.P r src)
    (hne : r ≠ src) (h : corr s.P src dst r = some x) :
    ∃ p p', parentOf s.P r = some p ∧ partOf s.P p src ∧ corr s.P src dst p = some p' ∧
      (kids s.P p')[posIn r (kids s.P p)]? = some x ∧ parentOf s.P x = some p' := by
  cases hp : parentOf s.P r with
  | none =>
    have hc := hr.2.resolve_left hne
    rw [chain_none hp] at hc; exact absurd hc List.not_mem_nil
  | some p =>
    have hlt := (hw.parent_lt hp).1
    rw [corr_step hne hp hlt] at h
    cases hc : corr s.P src dst p with
    | none => rw [hc] at h; cases h
    | some p' =>
      rw [hc] at h; simp only [Option.bind_some] at h
      exact ⟨p, p', rfl, partOf_parent hr hne hp hlt, rfl, h, (mem_kids.1 (getElem?_mem h)).2⟩

/-- `dst` is the image of no strict part of `src` (J1): the image of a strict part has as parent
a part of `dst`, which cannot be a parent of `dst`. -/
theorem corr_ne_dst {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst r : Nat} (hd : dst < s.P.length)
    (hr : partOf s.P r src) (hne : r ≠ src) : corr s.P src dst r ≠ some dst := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨p, p', -, -, hc, -, hx⟩ := corr_parent hw hr hne h
  have hlt := (hw.parent_lt hx).1
  rcases (corr_partOf hw hd (p + 1) p p' (Nat.lt_succ_self p) hc).2 with rfl | hch
  · exact Nat.lt_irrefl _ hlt
  · exact Nat.lt_asymm hlt (chain_lt hch)

/-- `corr` is injective on the parts of `src` (MM-03.3 O4.2, J1: all nodes are matched by
position, so two parts of `src` have the same image only if they are equal). -/
theorem corr_inj_aux {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hd : dst < s.P.length) :
    ∀ n r₁ r₂ x, r₁ + r₂ < n → partOf s.P r₁ src → partOf s.P r₂ src →
      corr s.P src dst r₁ = some x → corr s.P src dst r₂ = some x → r₁ = r₂
  | 0, _, _, _, h, _, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, r₁, r₂, x, hn, h₁, h₂, e₁, e₂ => by
    by_cases s₁ : r₁ = src <;> by_cases s₂ : r₂ = src
    · exact s₁.trans s₂.symm
    · subst s₁; rw [corr_src] at e₁; cases e₁
      exact absurd e₂ (corr_ne_dst hw hd h₂ s₂)
    · subst s₂; rw [corr_src] at e₂; cases e₂
      exact absurd e₁ (corr_ne_dst hw hd h₁ s₁)
    · obtain ⟨p₁, p₁', hp₁, hq₁, hc₁, hk₁, hx₁⟩ := corr_parent hw h₁ s₁ e₁
      obtain ⟨p₂, p₂', hp₂, hq₂, hc₂, hk₂, hx₂⟩ := corr_parent hw h₂ s₂ e₂
      rw [hx₁] at hx₂; cases hx₂
      have l₁ := (hw.parent_lt hp₁).1
      have l₂ := (hw.parent_lt hp₂).1
      obtain rfl := corr_inj_aux hw hd n p₁ p₂ p₁' (by omega) hq₁ hq₂ hc₁ hc₂
      exact posIn_inj (mem_kids.2 ⟨h₁.1, hp₁⟩) (mem_kids.2 ⟨h₂.1, hp₂⟩)
        (index_inj_of_lt (kids_lt _ _) hk₁ hk₂)

/-- The leaves of the source of a transfer correspond to leaves of the destination
(MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered isomorphism `SameShape`). -/
theorem corr_leaf_fwd {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hd : dst < s.P.length)
    (hsh : SameShape s.P src dst) {l : Nat} (hl : l ∈ footprint s.P src) :
    ∃ l', corr s.P src dst l = some l' ∧ l' ∈ footprint s.P dst := by
  obtain ⟨hlt, hleaf, hpart⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  have h1 := hsh.1 l (List.mem_range.2 hlt) hpart
  cases hc : corr s.P src dst l with
  | none => rw [hc] at h1; exact (h1 : False).elim
  | some l' =>
    rw [hc] at h1
    have h1 : (kids s.P l').length = (kids s.P l).length := h1
    rw [kids_nil_iff.2 hleaf] at h1
    have hp := corr_partOf hw hd (l + 1) l l' (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hc
    exact ⟨l', rfl, mem_footprint.2 ⟨hp.1, kids_nil_iff.1 (List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero h1), hp⟩⟩

/-- Every leaf of the destination of a transfer is the image of a leaf of the source
(MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered isomorphism `SameShape`: all nodes are matched). -/
theorem corr_leaf_back {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hsh : SameShape s.P src dst)
    {l' : Nat} (hl' : l' ∈ footprint s.P dst) :
    ∃ l ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l = some l' := by
  obtain ⟨hlt', hleaf', hpart'⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl'
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrs, hc⟩ := hsh.2 l' (List.mem_range.2 hlt') hpart'
  have h1 := hsh.1 r hr hrs
  rw [hc] at h1
  have h1 : (kids s.P l').length = (kids s.P r).length := h1
  rw [kids_nil_iff.2 hleaf'] at h1
  exact ⟨r, mem_footprint.2 ⟨List.mem_range.1 hr,
    kids_nil_iff.1 (List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero h1.symm), hrs⟩, hc⟩

/-- `corr` is injective on the parts of the source of a transfer (MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered
isomorphism: the `i`-th child corresponds to the `i`-th child). -/
theorem corr_inj {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hs : src < s.P.length)
    (hd : dst < s.P.length) (hno : ¬ overlap s.P src dst) {r₁ r₂ x : Nat}
    (h₁ : partOf s.P r₁ src) (h₂ : partOf s.P r₂ src) (e₁ : corr s.P src dst r₁ = some x)
    (e₂ : corr s.P src dst r₂ = some x) : r₁ = r₂ :=
  corr_inj_aux hw hd (r₁ + r₂ + 1) r₁ r₂ x (Nat.lt_succ_self _) h₁ h₂ e₁ e₂

#print axioms corr_leaf_fwd
#print axioms corr_leaf_back
#print axioms corr_inj
#print axioms posIn_inj
#print axioms index_inj_of_lt
#print axioms kids_lt
#print axioms partOf_parent
#print axioms corr_parent
#print axioms corr_ne_dst
#print axioms corr_inj_aux

end Ern.MM23

  simp only [posIn, h, ↓reduceIte]

theorem posIn_cons_ne {a r : Nat} {l : List Nat} (h : ¬ a = r) :
    posIn r (a :: l) = posIn r l + 1 := by
  simp only [posIn, h, ↓reduceIte]

/-- A position in a list determines the member it was computed for (MM-03.3 O4.2: the identity
of a structural field is its position). -/
theorem posIn_inj : ∀ {l : List Nat} {r₁ r₂ : Nat}, r₁ ∈ l → r₂ ∈ l →
    posIn r₁ l = posIn r₂ l → r₁ = r₂
  | [], _, _, h, _, _ => absurd h List.not_mem_nil
  | a :: l, r₁, r₂, h₁, h₂, e => by
    by_cases e₁ : a = r₁ <;> by_cases e₂ : a = r₂
    · exact e₁.symm.trans e₂
    · rw [posIn_cons_eq e₁, posIn_cons_ne e₂] at e; exact absurd e.symm (Nat.succ_ne_zero _)
    · rw [posIn_cons_ne e₁, posIn_cons_eq e₂] at e; exact absurd e (Nat.succ_ne_zero _)
    · rw [posIn_cons_ne e₁, posIn_cons_ne e₂] at e

      have h₂' : r₂ ∈ l := (List.mem_cons.1 h₂).resolve_left (Ne.symm e₂)
      exact posIn_inj h₁' h₂' (Nat.succ.inj e)

'''

/-- The leaves of the source of a transfer correspond to leaves of the destination
(MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered isomorphism `SameShape`). -/
theorem corr_leaf_fwd {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hd : dst < s.P.length)
    (hsh : SameShape s.P src dst) {l : Nat} (hl : l ∈ footprint s.P src) :
    ∃ l', corr s.P src dst l = some l' ∧ l' ∈ footprint s.P dst := by
  obtain ⟨hlt, hleaf, hpart⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  have h1 := hsh.1 l (List.mem_range.2 hlt) hpart
  cases hc : corr s.P src dst l with
  | none => rw [hc] at h1; exact (h1 : False).elim
  | some l' =>
    rw [hc] at h1
    have h1 : (kids s.P l').length = (kids s.P l).length := h1
    rw [kids_nil_iff.2 hleaf] at h1
    have hp := corr_partOf hw hd (l + 1) l l' (Nat.lt_succ_self l) hc
    exact ⟨l', rfl,
      mem_footprint.2 ⟨hp.1, kids_nil_iff.1 (List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero h1), hp⟩⟩

/-- Every leaf of the destination of a transfer is the image of a leaf of the source
(MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered isomorphism `SameShape`: all nodes are matched). -/
theorem corr_leaf_back {s : S3} (_hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hsh : SameShape s.P src dst)
    {l' : Nat} (hl' : l' ∈ footprint s.P dst) :
    ∃ l ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l = some l' := by
  obtain ⟨hlt', hleaf', hpart'⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl'
  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrs, hc⟩ := hsh.2 l' (List.mem_range.2 hlt') hpart'
  have h1 := hsh.1 r hr hrs
  rw [hc] at h1
  have h1 : (kids s.P l').length = (kids s.P r).length := h1
  rw [kids_nil_iff.2 hleaf'] at h1
  exact ⟨r, mem_footprint.2 ⟨List.mem_range.1 hr,
    kids_nil_iff.1 (List.eq_nil_of_length_eq_zero h1.symm), hrs⟩, hc⟩

/-- `corr` is injective on the parts of the source of a transfer (MM-03.3 O4.2, J1 ordered
isomorphism: the `i`-th child corresponds to the `i`-th child). -/
theorem corr_inj {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat}
    (_hs : src < s.P.length) (hd : dst < s.P.length) (_hno : ¬ overlap s.P src dst) {r₁ r₂ x : Nat}
    (h₁ : partOf s.P r₁ src) (h₂ : partOf s.P r₂ src) (e₁ : corr s.P src dst r₁ = some x)
    (e₂ : corr s.P src dst r₂ = some x) : r₁ = r₂ :=
  corr_inj_aux hw hd (r₁ + r₂ + 1) r₁ r₂ x (Nat.lt_succ_self _) h₁ h₂ e₁ e₂

**One change to the requested text:** three hypotheses that no proof uses now start with an underscore (`_hw`, `_hs`, `_hno`). Otherwise the unused-variable linter warns, and the repo already uses this convention (for example `_hwf` in MM03.lean:4963). The types are unchanged. Any caller that passes these arguments by name, such as `(hw := …)`, would need the new names.

Statements proved:
```lean
theorem corr_leaf_fwd {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hd : dst < s.P.length)
    (hsh : SameShape s.P src dst) {l : Nat} (hl : l ∈ footprint s.P src) :
    ∃ l', corr s.P src dst l = some l' ∧ l' ∈ footprint s.P dst

theorem corr_leaf_back {s : S3} (_hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat} (hsh : SameShape s.P src dst)
    {l' : Nat} (hl' : l' ∈ footprint s.P dst) :
    ∃ l ∈ footprint s.P src, corr s.P src dst l = some l'

theorem corr_inj {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {src dst : Nat}
    (_hs : src < s.P.length) (hd : dst < s.P.length) (_hno : ¬ overlap s.P src dst)
    {r₁ r₂ x : Nat} (h₁ : partOf s.P r₁ src) (h₂ : partOf s.P r₂ src)
    (e₁ : corr s.P src dst r₁ = some x) (e₂ : corr s.P src dst r₂ = some x) : r₁ = r₂
```

- **`corr_inj` needs no extra hypothesis, not even SameShape.** It also does not use `_hs` or `_hno`; it needs only `hw` and `hd`. The proof is by induction. The image of a strict part of `src` has a parent that is a part of `dst`, so that image is never `dst` itself. For two strict parts, equal images have the same parent, so their parents are equal by induction. The child lists are strictly increasing, so the same position means the same child.
- **`corr_leaf_back` does not use `WF3`.** It follows from the two clauses of `SameShape` alone.
